review_summary: The fix is narrow and mostly sound. Only exact same-repository GETs of git/{commits,trees,blobs}/<40 lowercase hex> are cached. Method, payload and query variants, refs, rulesets, Actions and PR paths stay fresh. Returns go through a canonical-bytes copy, so callers can't alias the cache. The foreign-API check runs before the cache lookup. On DeliveryAPI the 512-entry cap can never fire before the 512-call cap, so it adds no new limit. The one introduced defect is in QueueStore. Its immutable cache cap is cumulative over the object's lifetime, but its call and byte counters reset on every read() and checkpoint(). When the cache fills, the code raises instead of falling back to the old behaviour, so a run that used to fit within the per-operation budgets can now fail. The new tests don't exercise this path, and the foreign-API assertion is vacuous. The remaining findings are low-severity gating and test-strength gaps. This review covers only the supplied files and diff. I did not run anything or read factory-git-state.py, so the real GitState access pattern is unverified.

findings.title: QueueStore immutable cache cap is cumulative and fails hard, unlike the per-operation call/byte budgets it sits beside
findings.reason: read() and checkpoint() reset self.calls and self.consumed, so the 128-call and 32MiB budgets apply per operation. self.immutable and self.cached_bytes are never reset or evicted, so the new `len(self.immutable) < 128` and `cached_bytes+size <= 33554432` checks apply to the QueueStore's whole lifetime. run_queue reuses one QueueStore across read(), several checkpoint() calls (each does up to 3 attempts of two _load() calls) and every new head. Each new head adds fresh commit, tree and blob objects, and a nonfast-forward CAS retry adds more. Once 128 unique immutable objects have been seen, the next uncached one raises 'queue immutable cache bound exceeded', after the provider call was already made and charged. The old code allowed 128 calls on every operation. Because this is a new failure mode, 'all limits preserved' isn't strictly true. The README's recovery run used 74 source calls in total, so the fixture stays under the cap, but production state history is not bounded by that fixture. Fix: when the cache is full, return the value uncached (keep the existing call and byte charging) instead of raising. Or clear the cache whenever read() and checkpoint() reset the counters. DeliveryAPI is unaffected because its calls counter never resets, so its cache cap can't fire before the call cap.

findings.title: QueueStore and DeliveryAPI use different cache gates; QueueStore is not limited to archive mode
findings.reason: DeliveryAPI.__init__ (line 404) caches only when state_view.mode == 'archive'. QueueStore.request caches whenever storage.get('state_view') is not None. If state_view_config accepts any other mode, QueueStore would cache outside the stated archive-only scope. I couldn't confirm which modes it accepts because factory-git-state.py wasn't supplied. Align the two gates, preferably on the validated mode, and add a test with a present but non-archive state_view.

findings.title: Foreign-API assertions run against an exhausted adapter, so they can't fail for the intended reason
findings.reason: By line 39 `bounded` has used all 512 calls. Any uncached request, foreign or not, raises ValueError from the call bound. The `except ValueError: pass` therefore passes even if the same-repository check is removed or reordered. Run the foreign and prefix-confusion paths ('repos/foreign/repo/...', 'repos/org/repository/...') on a fresh adapter and assert the message contains 'foreign API'. QueueStore has no foreign-path test at all.

findings.title: New cache-bound error paths and cross-operation behaviour are untested
findings.reason: The 128 and 512 unique-call tests hit the call bound first (`API bound exceeded`), because calls are checked before the cache and both caps are 128 or 512. 'queue immutable cache bound exceeded' is never reached in either class. The 32MiB and 64MiB cache-byte caps are untested, and so is a cache hit not adding to consumed. Nothing tests the main QueueStore risk: cache persistence across read() and checkpoint() while the call and byte counters reset. Add a test that makes more than 128 unique immutable reads across several read() calls. Also add negative regex cases: uppercase or 39/41-character hex, a trailing slash, a /extra suffix, and git/tags or git/refs.

findings.title: DeliveryAPI cache-bound check is redundant and unreachable
findings.reason: calls is cumulative and capped at 512, and consumed is capped at 67108864. So len(self.immutable) < 512 and cached_bytes+size <= 67108864 can never fail first. The check is harmless but gives a false impression of an independent bound, and it is untested. Either drop it or note that it is defensive.

limitations: Review is static and limited to the supplied files and diff. I executed no code and did not run the tests.

factory-git-state.py, factory-reporting-alerts.py, the slack/digest modules and the real transport were not supplied. I could not check which state_view modes are valid, how many unique immutable objects GitState fetches per load, or whether any caller depends on commit fields that can change over time, such as `verification`. That would matter if a caller checks signatures. Content-addressed commit, tree and blob bodies are otherwise immutable.

The README reports 503 provider calls for scheduled recovery against the 512 DeliveryAPI limit. The README doesn't say whether that total includes cache hits. Headroom looks thin, and larger real state or a CAS retry could still hit the limit. This fix reduces redundant charging but does not show the path has comfortable margin.

I did not verify the README's claims about the real-Git, concurrent-CAS and Slack-receipt negative tests. No native App, cadence or live-API claim is made here, and PASS would cover only the supplied scope.
